issue_request: FHIR-22807 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I correction for the CodeSystem $lookup OperationDefinition. It reported that the narrative listed property.value and property.subproperty.value as a choice of code, Coding, string, integer, boolean, dateTime, and decimal, while the formal operation definition exposed only code. The updated resolution called for the R4 allowed-type extension and an R5 OperationDefinition parameter element for allowed concrete subtypes of an abstract parameter type.
initial_application: Commit 299a6a9e9de2c85b252bb219aaee66da4be7ab2e explicitly applied FHIR-22807 by adding OperationDefinition.parameter.allowedType, using the final current element name rather than the Jira resolution's draft name of subtype. The lookup operation source already carried the R4-style operationdefinition-allowed-type extensions when source/codesystem/operationdefinition-CodeSystem-lookup.xml was introduced in 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157.
additional_context: CodeSystem and OperationDefinition are active resources in source/fhir.ini. Later operation-definition refactoring in 646720401223f784271c0f6c478484a47094dc06 converted the lookup operation's allowed-type extensions to native allowedType elements while preserving the concrete type list for both affected value parts. FHIR-52921 later clarified profile alignment around type and allowedType lists. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source already matches the intended formal operation surface: property.value and property.subproperty.value are type Element with allowedType entries for Coding, boolean, code, dateTime, decimal, integer, and string.
